title: Wave suggest keeps engine slices apart: at most one engine, daemon or cmd slice per suggested wave
lead: *Proposed.* `ork wave suggest` and the Waves screen defer every second slice whose Files touch `internal/engine`, `internal/daemon` or `cmd` out of a suggested wave into a wave of its own right after it, so every suggested wave can be launched as shown. Today the owner finds the conflict only after ticking, or when the daemon refuses the wave.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Friction found in the v1.1 prescan (2026-10-31). The rule exists: "A wave may contain at most one slice whose Files touch `internal/engine`, `internal/daemon` or `cmd`" (`docs/design.md:1765-1768`; adj 166 `engine.self-host`, decided: main-binary-restart). The daemon enforces it at `wave.start` with `EngineSlice` (`internal/daemon/build.go:43-65`) and `EngineConflict` (`:67-70`), called from `startWave` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:685-699`), and the Waves screen marks it after the owner ticks two such items and plans them (`engineConflict`, `internal/tui/waves.go:865-878`; S114 and S125, both done in `slicer list --all`). The suggestion itself does not know the rule. `wave.suggest` returns slicer's `plan-parallel` result unchanged (`internal/daemon/reads.go:53-61`), and `ork wave suggest` calls slicer directly (`internal/cli/wave.go:50`).

Evidence from 2026-10-31: `slicer plan-parallel --json --lean --root .` puts S129, S67, S50 and S128 in wave 1. All four list a path under `internal/engine`, `internal/daemon` or `cmd` in their Files, so the daemon would refuse that wave. Pair planning for v1.1 is "one engine slice plus one other slice per wave", and the owner currently pairs by hand.

Slicer check: `slicer --root ../slicer find plan-parallel` lists s376, s377 and s395 only; none adds a path-class rule. plan-parallel places items by exact shared `files_section` paths less `overlap_ignore` (`../slicer/docs/commands.md:35`) and does not know ork's directory-level rule. `slicer show ID --json` returns `paths` (s395, done; `../slicer/docs/agents.md`, `show ID` row), but ork's `EngineSlice` reads the Files section text, so this slice keeps using `EngineSlice`.

Boundary: `docs/boundaries.md` lists wave suggestion as slicer's (`wave.selection`). This slice makes ork reorder slicer's suggestion by ork's own self-hosting rule (adj 166), which is the owner's call (MANIFEST-E.md, SE-Q1).

Scope of the reshaping, the default of this outline (SE-Q2): the extra engine slice goes alone into a new wave inserted right after the wave it came from. It never moves into an existing later wave, so no overlap or dependency read is needed and no dependency order can break: an item that waited on it still comes after it. The cost is that a deferred engine slice runs alone unless the owner adds a non-engine slice by hand. Filling the deferred slice into a later wave with room is a larger change (it needs `slicer deps --overlap` and dependency reads per placement); it is listed as option b in the manifest.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
This slice touches `internal/daemon` and `internal/cli`: it is an E-class slice (at most one such slice per wave). It also changes the Waves reason text and ork wave suggest output (UI).

- `internal/daemon/waveengine.go` (new): ApplyEngineRule(plan, engine) (pure) and SuggestWithEngineRule(ctx, shower, root, plan), which reads each placed item with Show and calls EngineSlice (`internal/daemon/build.go:91`).
- `internal/daemon/waveengine_test.go` (new).
- `internal/daemon/reads.go:53-69` (waveSuggest calls it) and `internal/daemon/daemon_test.go:1320-1350` (TestWaveSuggestReturnsPlanParallel counts only the plan-parallel calls, because the show reads are extra; both TestWaveSuggest* tests keep passing).
- `internal/cli/wave.go:32-60` (waveSuggest calls the same function) and `internal/cli/wave_test.go:37-140`.
- `internal/tui/waves.go:770` (waveReason words for the new reason), `internal/tui/waves_test.go`, and the new goldens `testdata/golden/waves-engine-100x30-mono.txt` and `testdata/golden/waves-engine-80x24-mono.txt`.
- `docs/design.md` (the wave.suggest row of the wire table; the Self-hosting section, where the rule says a wave may contain at most one such slice), `docs/dashboard.md` (Waves (one project): reason words and the CLI paragraph), `docs/boundaries.md` (Ownership row "Wave suggestion"), `docs/guide.md` (section 9, Run a wave).
- `CHANGELOG.md` (an entry under ## Unreleased, marked *proposed*).

`internal/slicercli` is not changed: ParallelItem.Reason already carries free text.

Pair planning: E-class (`internal/daemon`). Do not pair with another E-class slice. It can pair with an N-class slice that does not edit `internal/tui/waves.go`, `docs/design.md` or `docs/dashboard.md`. It touches `internal/cli/wave.go` like the named wave does, so do not put the two in one wave even though only one is E-class by the engine rule alone (both are E-class here).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
`internal/daemon/waveengine_test.go` (the function does not exist: compile error first):
- `TestApplyEngineRuleLeavesAPlanWithOneEngineSlicePerWaveUnchanged`: output equals input, including reasons and wave numbers (a copy, not the same pointer).
- `TestApplyEngineRuleKeepsTheFirstEngineSliceOfAWaveAndDefersTheRest`: wave 1 `[E1,E2,N1,E3]` becomes wave 1 `[E1,N1]`, wave 2 `[E2]`, wave 3 `[E3]`, then the old wave 2 becomes wave 4; slicer item order is kept; the input is not edited.
- `TestApplyEngineRuleRenumbersWaves`: wave numbers run 1..n with no gap, also for gapped input.
- `TestApplyEngineRuleDeferredItemsGetTheEngineReason`: the reason is `engine: E1` (the engine slice kept in the wave it came from), replacing the old reason (*proposed* wording).
- `TestApplyEngineRuleKeepsDependencyOrder`: an item whose reason was `after: E2` still sits in a wave after E2 new wave, and E2 sits right after E1.
- `TestApplyEngineRuleDoesNotTouchUnplacedBlockedHeldOrInFlight`: those lists are copied as they are; an in-flight engine slice does not count against a wave.
- `TestApplyEngineRuleIsStable`: applying it twice gives the same plan.
- `TestSuggestWithEngineRuleReadsEachPlacedItemOnce`: the fake records one `show` per placed item and none for unplaced, blocked, held or unspecified items.
- `TestSuggestWithEngineRuleSkipsReadsWhenEveryWaveHoldsOneItem`: no `show` read when no wave has a second item.
- `TestSuggestWithEngineRuleReadsInParallelButKeepsOrder`: eight reads in flight at once, never more; results do not depend on completion order (run with `-race`).
- `TestSuggestWithEngineRuleFailedReadLeavesThatItemAlone`: a `show` error makes that item count as not an engine slice; the call still succeeds (the start-time check in `startWave` remains the guard).
- `TestWaveSuggestRequestDefersEngineSlices` (via wire JSON): `wave.suggest` returns the reshaped plan.
- `TestWaveSuggestWithNoEngineSlicesIsByteIdenticalToSlicer`: the recorded plan comes back byte for byte.

`internal/cli/wave_test.go`:
- `TestWaveSuggestDefersASecondEngineSlice`: text output shows the deferred item in its own wave with `(engine: E1)`; `--json` carries the same reason.
- `TestWaveSuggestStillWorksWithoutAShowRoute`: when the fake slicer cannot answer `show`, the output is slicer plan (fail open).

`internal/tui/waves_test.go`:
- `TestWaveReasonExplainsTheEngineRule`: `waveReason("engine: S129")` reads `one engine slice per wave; S129 goes first`. Existing Waves goldens do not change (their fixtures hold no engine reason).
- `TestWavesShowsADeferredEngineSliceInItsOwnWave` (new goldens, 100x30 mono and 80x24 mono).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Tests first. Do not touch: `EngineSlice`, `EngineConflict` or the start-time refusal in `startWave` (they stay as the guard); the Waves screen's own conflict mark; `internal/slicercli` types; slicer data.

1. Preflight: SE-Q1 and SE-Q2 are answered. If SE-Q1 is "mark only" or "slicer option", stop: this outline does not apply.
2. Write the tests above.
3. `ApplyEngineRule`: walk `plan.Waves` in order. In each wave keep the first item whose id is in `engine`; for every further engine item, remove it and put it alone in a new wave inserted directly after the current wave, in slicer's item order, with `Reason: "engine: " + keptID`. Process the inserted waves in turn (each holds one item, so they need nothing more). Renumber `Wave` 1..n at the end. Return a copy; never mutate slicer's slices in place. Items of `Unplaced`, `Blocked`, `Held`, `Unspecified` and `InFlight` are copied as they are.
4. `SuggestWithEngineRule(ctx, shower, root, plan)`: `shower` is a small interface with `Show(ctx, root, id) (*slicercli.Detail, error)`, satisfied by `slicercli.Client`. Read each placed item with `Show` at most 8 at a time (12 sequential `slicer show` calls took 1.1 s on 2026-10-31, so a plan of 25 placed items would add about 2 s if read one by one), call `EngineSlice`, then `ApplyEngineRule`. Skip the reads when no wave has more than one item. A read error leaves that item as non-engine.
5. Wire it in `waveSuggest` (`reads.go`) and in the CLI's `waveSuggest` (`wave.go:50`), using `d.runs.deps.Slicer` and `slicercli.Client{Bin: a.Tools.Slicer}` respectively.
6. `waveReason` in `internal/tui/waves.go`: map `engine: ID` to the plain words. Nothing else in the table changes; the Shares column is only for `shares:` reasons (`waveShares`, `:881-891`).
7. Docs, *proposed*: the sentence in `docs/design.md:1765-1768` gains "`wave.suggest` and `ork wave suggest` put a second such slice in a wave of its own after the first"; the dashboard Waves text gains the reason; the boundaries row says ork defers engine slices in slicer's suggestion by the self-hosting rule.
8. CHANGELOG entry last, under `## Unreleased`: `Wave suggest and the engine rule (*proposed*): ...`. Add it as the final edit so a parallel slice's entry does not conflict.

UI slice: UI pass (r14).

Owner decisions: 2026-11-07 (interview). SE-Q1: ork may reorder slicer's suggestion; this is a documented exception to showing it as is. SE-Q2: a deferred engine slice goes alone into a new wave.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/daemon ./internal/cli ./internal/tui`.
- `ork wave suggest ork` on this repo (after the build) shows no wave with two items that `internal/daemon.EngineSlice` flags; compare with `slicer plan-parallel --json --lean --root .` to see what moved.
- [HUMAN CHECK] At 100x30 and 80x24 in a live terminal: open Waves on a project with several engine slices and read the deferred items' reason lines; confirm opening the screen is not noticeably slower (it adds the parallel `show` reads).

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Wave suggest: keep a second engine, daemon or cmd slice out of the wave".
